CONNAUGHT RD. BUS
INCIDENT

Case Against Chauffeur to
Go to Nantao Court

OUTSIDE ROAD QUESTION
INVOLVED

Holding that the Connaught Road bus accident of April 7, when the Chapei police interfered with the Settlement police who attempted to remove the victim of the accident, a Chinese cyclist, occurred on an "outside road," Judge Wu Chih-han of the First Special District Court yesterday announced that the Settlement Chinese court had no jurisdiction over the private criminal case brought by the killed cyclist's father against the bus company chauffeur and instructed that the case be transferred to the Nantao District Court for trial.

The case in question came up for resumed hearing yesterday morning. When the Court started its session, Judge Wu asked the complainant, Sun Ming-tsang, whether he also wished to bring any civil claim against the bus chauffeur. The complainant replied that he would bring the civil claim against the China General Omnibus Co., the chauffeur's employers, whereupon the Judge told the complainant that this could not be done in the Chinese court because the China General Omnibus Co. was a British firm enjoying extraterritorial privileges in China.

After consultation with his lawyer, the complainant withdrew his civil claim against the bus company, but said he reserved his right to bring a similar claim against the chauffeur.

Agreement Cited

As regards the question of jurisdiction, Judge Wu said he had visited last Wednesday morning the scene of the accident and found it had occurred on an "outside road." In accordance with the Rendition Agreement provisions, Judge Wu continued only "mixed cases," namely, cases involving foreigners, that had occurred on outside roads would be accepted by his Court for hearing. As both parties in this case were Chinese, the case should be dealt with by the Nantao District Court.

The complainant again consulted his lawyer and then he told the Judge that he had decided to withdraw the criminal case against the bus chauffeur in the Settlement Chinese court and would bring the matter to the Nantao District Court.

Mr. Y. D. Wong, Assistant Municipal Advocate, watched the case for the Municipal Police. 事件

针对司机的案件将
移交南市法院审理

涉及“越界筑路”问题

第一特区地方法院法官吴志涵昨日裁定，4月7日发生的康纳路公共汽车事故中，当租界巡捕试图移走事故受害者（一名中国骑自行车者）时，闸北警方进行了干涉，该事故发生在“越界筑路”地段，因此租界华界法庭对死者父亲提起的针对公交公司司机的私人刑事诉讼无管辖权，并指示将该案移交南市地方法院审理。

上述案件于昨日上午恢复审理。开庭时，吴法官询问原告孙明藏（音译），是否也希望对公交司机提出任何民事索赔。原告答复称，他将对司机的雇主——中国通用公共汽车公司（China General Omnibus Co.）提出民事索赔，对此法官告知原告，此举无法在华界法庭进行，因为中国通用公共汽车公司是一家在中国享有治外法权的英国公司。

在与律师商议后，原告撤回了对公交公司的民事索赔，但表示保留对司机提出类似索赔的权利。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SUNDAY, APRIL 22, 1934

CONNAUGHT RD. BUS
INCIDENT

Legal Proceedings Against
Bus Driver

JUDGE TO VISIT SCENE
OF ACCIDENT

The question of jurisdiction over the "Connaught Road bus accident case" of April 7, when the removal of the victim of an accident, a Chinese cyclist, was delayed by the officers of Public Safety Bureau, came in for heated argument in the First Special District Court yesterday, when a private criminal prosecution was instituted against Wong Tsang-kuei, the bus driver concerned in the accident, by Sun Ming-tsang, father of the killed cyclist.

When the case was opened before Judge Wu Cheh-han, two officers from the Public Safety Bureau were called as witnesses and they maintained that the place where the accident occurred was within Chinese-controlled territory. One of the officers, a constable named Li Teh-kuei, 32, said that Connaught Road was an outside road and that he was on duty about 150 metres from the place of accident on April 7. Tsien Yoh-fong, an inspector of the Public Safety Bureau, told the Judge that although water and electricity to Connaught Road residents were supplied by the Settlement companies, the place of the bus accident of April 7 was entirely within Chinese controlled territory and that all traffic cases on this road had been hitherto handled by the Public Safety authorities.

The complainant, in answer to the Judge, stated, however, that the Shanghai Municipal Council collected the general rates from the residents of that road.

Decision Withheld

On the basis of the statements of the two Public Safety officers, a verbal ruling was given by Judge Wu that the case was not under this Court's jurisdiction. This ruling, however, drew a strong protest from Mr. V. T. Van, lawyer for the driver, who declared that the question of jurisdiction could not be determined simply on the basis of the statements of two Public Safety officers without seeking further evidence.

After further questioning of the complainant, the accused and the two Public Safety officers as to whether the scene of the accident was within the Chinese-controlled territory, the Judge gave a written decision that the hearing would be adjourned until he had paid a visit to the scene of the accident, it being pointed out that the case could not be proceeded with without first settling the question of jurisdiction. When the Judge will visit the place was not announced yesterday.

康纳路公共汽车
事件

对公交车司机的
法律诉讼

法官将视察
事故现场

4月7日“康纳路公共汽车事故案”的管辖权问题昨日在第一特区地方法院引发激烈辩论，当时遇难骑车人之父孙明藏（音译）对涉案公交车司机王藏贵（Wong Tsang-kuei, 音译）提起了私人刑事控告。在该事故中，公安当局警官延误了移走事故受害者（一名中国骑车人）。

案件在吴哲涵（Wu Cheh-han, 音译）法官面前开庭时，两名公安局警官被传唤为证人，他们坚称事故发生地位于中国管辖区域内。其中一名警官，32岁的巡捕李德贵（Li Teh-kuei, 音译）称，康纳路是一条越界筑路，4月7日他在距离事故地点约150米处执勤。公安局督察钱耀芳（Tsien Yoh-fong, 音译）告诉法官，虽然康纳路居民的水电由租界公司供应，但4月7日公共汽车事故的地点完全位于中国管辖区域内，且迄今为止该道路上的所有交通案件均由公安当局处理。

然而，原告在回答法官提问时表示，上海工部局向该路居民征收一般捐税。

暂缓裁决

基于两名公安局警官的陈述，吴法官口头裁定该案不属于本庭管辖。然而，这一裁决遭到了司机辩护律师范特（V. T. Van, 音译）先生的强烈抗议，他宣称，在不寻求进一步证据的情况下，仅凭两名公安局警官的陈述无法确定管辖权问题。

在对原告、被告及两名公安局警官就事故现场是否位于中国管辖区域内进行进一步讯问后，法官作出书面决定，宣布休庭，直至其亲自视察事故现场，并指出在未首先解决管辖权问题之前，案件无法继续进行。法官何时前往该地，昨日并未公布。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Tuesday, April 17, 1934.

On Connaught Road
To the Editor:
I cannot say that I read with amazement the article in your issue of the 14th April by Kwei Chungshu on the Connaught Road accident. The heading "As a Chinese Sees It" dispelled the possible amazement which the article may have caused.
Kwei Chungshu appears to be a little vague as to the issue at stake. In Para. 4 he writes. "The main issue centers around the condition of the victim immediately after the accident." In Para. 10 he states that the blus to the whole agitation lies as to whether a hue and cry would have been raised had the accident happened in the Settlement.
Kwei Chungshu drags the Sino-Japanese skeleton out of the cupboard in an attempt to hit at a daily contemporary and concludes his article with blaming the Japanese for obstructing the outside roads question. Kwei Chungshu would probably have us to believe that the Japanese were to blame directly or indirectly for the incident arising out of the Connaught Road accident.
According to Chinese law, as quoted by Kwei Chungshu, a man is dead when visible breathing has stopped. (Italics are mine). Does this mean that if a person is not seen by the naked eye to be breathing he is dead? If so, I would not like to be in a trance under a Chinese doctor or lawyer.
Kwei Chungshu's "common sense view," that the victim's death must have been immediate, because a vehicle weighing 12,000 lbs. had run over his chest, cannot be taken for granted. One must remember the numerous cases on record where a person has received terrible injuries and has still survived. There are persons living who have broken necks and who should, according to Kwei Chungshu's "common sense," be rigid in death. I would like to cite the case of the U. S. Marine, who in this very city a few days ago, received gun shot wounds in the head via the mouth, became unconscious, regained consciousness and walked up a flight of steps, before collapsing again.
Death to the victim of the bus accident is, to quote Kwei Chungshu, doubly certain by testimonials of witnesses. He undoubtedly means the witnesses for the Chinese police. He must not forget the other witnesses who state that the victim did not die instantaneously. Much sounder common sense than Kwei Chungshu's is contained in the following sentence. A dead man cannot groan.
The deceased's mother has everyone's sympathy, but on the other hand I would like to suggest that the mother could not claim compensation from the Bus Co., if she agreed that death was not instantaneous and could possibly have been averted if the Chinese police had allowed the immediate removal of her son.
If the victim was still alive, Kwei Chungshu asks, why did not the kind-hearted Municipal Police take hold of the situation and remove him in spite of the objections of the Chinese Police? He then goes on to state that "One wonders why these 'humanitarian' brothers of mercy hesitated to employ force with force, but chose to remain as tame lambs—" (Belief are mine). I ask Kwei Chungshu if he honestly believes that the Chinese law would have upheld the Municipal Police if the above combat had taken place?

Kwei Chungshu's previous question is ably answered by that "certain contemporary" who, if I may be permitted to quote state—something might have started which would probably have proceeded far beyond control; and a very unfortunate affair transformed into a tragedy on a much larger scale."
It is amusing to read Kwei Chung-shu's question which commences, "If the incident had happened within the Settlement." In conclusion, I ask Kwei Chungshu to state since when was Connaught Road not part of the Settlement road, why are the street name posts printed in foreign and Chinese and not Chinese alone?
LAU-BOO-SAH.
Shanghai, April 16, 1934.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1934年4月17日，星期二。

致编辑：关于康纳路

我并不能说我怀着惊讶的心情阅读了贵报4月14日刊载的桂中枢（Kwei Chungshu, 音译）关于康纳路事故的文章。标题“一个中国人的看法”消除了文章可能引起的任何惊讶。

桂中枢似乎对争议焦点有些模糊不清。在第4段中他写道：“主要问题集中在事故发生后受害者的状况。”在第10段中，他指出，整个骚动的症结在于，如果事故发生在租界内，是否会引发一片哗然。

桂中枢搬出中日关系的陈年旧账，试图攻击一家日报，并在文章结尾指责日本人阻碍了越界筑路问题的解决。桂中枢大概想让我们相信，日本人应对康纳路事故引发的这一事件负直接或间接责任。

根据桂中枢引用的中国法律，当可见的呼吸停止时，人即死亡。（着重号为本人所加）。这是否意味着，如果肉眼未看到某人呼吸，他就已经死亡？如果是这样，我可不愿在中国医生或律师手下处于假死状态。

桂中枢所谓的“常识观点”认为，鉴于车辆重达12,000磅并碾过受害者胸部，其死亡必然是即刻发生的，这种观点不能想当然。人们必须记住，记录在案中有许多案例显示，人员遭受可怕伤害后仍然幸存。有些颈部骨折的人至今尚在人世，而按照桂中枢的“常识”，他们本该僵直死去。我想引用一名美国海军陆战队士兵的案例，就在几天前，在这座城市里，他头部经口腔遭受枪伤，失去知觉，后又恢复知觉，并走上了一段楼梯，之后才再次倒下。

引用桂中枢的话说，目击证人的证词使公共汽车事故受害者的死亡加倍确凿。他无疑是指中方警方的证人。他一定不要忘记其他声称受害者并非立即死亡的证人。下面这句话所包含的常识比桂中枢的更为可靠：死人不会呻吟。

死者的母亲值得所有人同情，但另一方面，我想指出，如果这位母亲同意死亡并非即时发生，且若中国警方允许立即移走其儿子或许本可避免死亡，那么她就无法向公共汽车公司索赔。

如果受害者当时还活着，桂中枢问道，为何仁慈的工部局巡捕不接管局面，不顾中国警方的反对将其移走？他接着陈述道：“人们不禁要问，这些‘人道主义’的慈善兄弟为何犹豫不决，不以武力对抗武力，却选择像温顺的羔羊一样——”（信念为本人所加）。我问桂中枢，他是否真诚地相信，如果发生上述冲突，中国法律会支持工部局巡捕？

桂中枢先前提出的问题得到了那家“某当代报纸”的有力回答，如果允许我引用的话，该报称——“可能会引发某种事态，其发展很可能远远超出控制范围；一件非常不幸的事情将演变成规模大得多的悲剧。”

读到桂中枢以“如果事件发生在租界内”开头的问题，颇觉有趣。最后，我问桂中枢，请说明从何时起康纳路不再是租界道路的一部分，为何路名牌是用外文和中文印刷，而不是仅用中文？

刘布萨（LAU-BOO-SAH, 音译）。
上海，1934年4月16日。

CONNAUGHT ROAD INCIDENT REFUTED

Editor, THE CHINA PRESS,
Sir:—After more than a week of fruitless dispute between The China General Omnibus Company and the Chapel police, the horrible accident in which a Chinese cyclist was knocked down and pinned underneath the bus (Settlement license No. 15007) along Connaught Road shortly after 8 p.m. on April 7, is still a thorny question before the Chinese and Settlement authorities in this city.

Involving the question of extra-Settlement roads, this incident is particularly delicate and significant from a technical point of view. But no matter how the authorities concerned will settle this problem, all sensible residents in Shanghai must at least have a fair sense of comparison of facts as they are.

The verdict reads:

Mr. "Disgusted"
Evidently, Mr. "Disgusted" must have a high discretionary power, otherwise he would not have chosen such a grand occasion to make his debut in the paper. Ordinary people with a little common sense could easily see whether or not the story published with such an exaggeration three days after the incident is of any good intention.

In the first place, as a leading paper here, the North China Daily News should be responsible for releasing the story in such a misleading manner. The reporter who collected the news must have accomplished a lot after three days of elaborate investigation. The most important thing we would like to know in a case like this is the part of the body over which the heavy wheel of the omnibus rested. Most likely, the paper purposely left out this most significant point in order to justify its incredible fabrication. A thousand pounds heaped on the chest of any ordinary person will be sufficient to stop his breath in one or two seconds. If the man could still be "shrieking from pain" after six minutes when the Settlement ambulance was said to have arrived, he would have survived the crash to thank the papers for taking the trouble to publish the story on his account.

How About Victim's Mother
Again, the North China Daily News has failed to say anything about the victim's mother, who, in addition to her great sorrow for the bereavement of her only son had to stand the insult at the hand of a foreign officer in the Gordon Road Station. If the Chapel police were so barbarous as has been alleged, nobody would believe that the mother of the victim could allow her son still "shrieking from pain" to be kept under the wheel without either making any effort to rescue him or condemning the Chinese police for their torturing action.

After interviewing a few of the eye-witnesses and after following closely all sides of the controversy in the papers during the last eight days, the writer cannot refrain from entertaining suspicion of the good intention of the North China Daily News in its publication of the story. Many foreign residents in Shanghai will be disappointed at the steps thus taken by their representative paper in needlessly arousing antagonistic feeling among Chinese and foreigners in this city, the peace and order of which depend to a large extent upon the goodwill and mutual understanding of all.

If the North China Daily News thinks that the Chinese authorities should be deprived of their jurisdiction over the extra-Settlement roads, it should pick out a better occasion to air it can just speak out frankly and the Chinese will be grateful for its straightforwardness. They voluntarily surrender the sovereignty of their country.

Yours etc.,
C. K. CHEN.

康纳路事件之驳斥

致《字林西报》编辑：
先生：——在上海公共汽车公司（The China General Omnibus Company）与巡捕房警察经过一周多徒劳无益的争执之后，4月7日晚8点过后不久，在康纳路（Connaught Road）发生的一起可怕事故——一名中国骑自行车者被撞倒并被压在一辆公共汽车（租界牌照第15007号）之下——仍然是本市中方当局与租界当局面前一个棘手的问题。

由于涉及越界筑路问题，从技术角度来看，这一事件尤为微妙且意义重大。但无论有关当局如何解决这一问题，上海所有理智的居民至少必须对事实真相有一个公平的比较认知。

判决如下：
4月8日，5弄1号的美国当局将尸体带回家，并持有一把.38口径的柯尔特左轮手枪，以谋杀罪在第一分院法庭受审。一位名为Thomas C. Woo（音译）的华裔知名人士被判刑，死因为自杀。

自杀裁决
百老汇路〔此处转录不清〕后俄国乞丐之死
自杀 N

展示由中国警察强行阻止立即给予救助。”

“厌恶”先生
显然，“厌恶”先生一定拥有很高的裁量权，否则他不会选择如此盛大的场合在报纸上首次亮相。稍有常识的普通人很容易看出，在事件发生三天后以如此夸张的方式发布的故事是否怀有任何善意。

首先，作为本地的一家主要报纸，《字林西报》应对以这种误导性方式发布新闻负责。收集该新闻的记者在经过三天的精心调查后，一定取得了不少成果。在此类案件中，我们最想知道的是公共汽车沉重的车轮压在身体的哪个部位。很可能，该报故意遗漏了这一最重要的要点，以使其令人难以置信的捏造显得合理。任何普通人的胸口若被压上一千磅的重物，足以在一两秒钟内使其停止呼吸。如果当据说租界救护车到达时，此人在六分钟后仍能“痛苦地尖叫”，那他本该在那次撞击中幸存下来，并感谢报纸费心为他刊登这篇报道。

受害者母亲的情况如何
此外，《字林西报》只字未提受害者的母亲，她不仅在失去独子的巨大悲痛中，还要忍受戈登路（Gordon Road）警局一名外籍警官的侮辱。如果巡捕房警察真如指控那般野蛮，没人会相信受害者的母亲会让儿子继续“痛苦地尖叫”而被压在车轮下，既不努力施救，也不谴责中国警察的折磨行为。

在采访了几位目击者，并在过去八天里密切关注报纸上各方争议后，笔者不禁怀疑《字林西报》发布该报道的善意。许多在上海的外国居民会对他们的代表性报纸采取此类步骤感到失望，因为这无端激起了本市中外居民之间的对立情绪，而本市的和平与秩序在很大程度上取决于所有人的善意与相互理解。

如果《字林西报》认为中国当局应被剥夺对越界筑路的管辖权，它应该选择一个更好的时机来宣扬这一观点，或者干脆坦率直言，中国人会感激其直率。他们自愿放弃自己国家的主权。

此致，
C. K. CHEN.
1934年4月16日。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, APRIL 17, 1941

CONNAUGHT RD. SCANDAL
Some Cool Thinking
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—As popular interest in the
"Connaught Road Incident" would
seem, judging from the space it oc-
cupies in your correspondence co-
lumns, not waning, but rather increas-
ing, on account of the mutual re-
criminations indulged in by various
readers who have aligned themselves
on one side or the other, may I
request again a little space to ask for
a little more cool thinking from those
impulsive persons who would hurry
to condemn before they have heard
the whole case.
I would like merely to call atten-
tion to a crucial point which has
rather been lost sight of because
"racial prejudices," "outside roads"
and other irrelevant questions involv-
ing mutual washing of dirty linen
have generated so much heat that the
real issues have been lost sight of in
the haze.
It is an axiom that the person who
makes a statement shall be prepared,
if called upon, to substantiate it. It
is the duty, therefore, of those who
contend that the unfortunate victim
of the accident was not killed out-
right, to bring forth the strongest evi-
dence they possess to sustain their
allegation since the same has been
traversed. Once their case is made
out, then it will be time to call upon
the Bureau of Public Safety to ex-
plain whatever there is to explain. I
am not trying to take up the cudgels
on behalf of the Bureau, and would
wholeheartedly join in its condemna-
tion if the allegations against the
Bureau were all true. But I have
noticed that all reports have been
strangely silent over the official death
certificate or the result of the coro-
ner's inquiry. Yet that is the crux
of the whole affair. A passing re-
ference in the Omnibus Company's
statement, appearing in your columns
on April 13, mentioned that "the cause
of death was shock." Everybody
knows that a person who succumbs to
injuries received in an accident in-
variably suffers from shock to some
extent. The vital part of the medical
testimony, however, that is missing is
shock as the result of what injuries?
Certain injuries do cause instantaneous
death, and the medical evidence would
perhaps be able instantly to dispel
all the hot air that is blown about
over this case.
F. T. WANG.
Shanghai, Apr. 16.
***The evidence that the victim of
the accident did live a considerable
time after the accident has been pub-
lished in these columns and is over-
whelming. One witness saw the un-
fortunate young man's arms and legs
move. The Chinese Officer Cadet in
charge of the Fire Brigade ambulance
appealed to Mr. Shotton: "Mr. Shot-
ton, for God's sake can't you do any-
thing to get the man out, so maybe
we can save his life." Another witness
actually felt the victim's pulse beating
and he was also breathing. A fourth
witness saw the arms and legs moving,
saw the man eventually close his eyes
and apparently die. That was at 9.20
p.m., twenty-nine minutes after the
accident. While there is every reason
care of opinion as to whether the
victim groaned or moaned during all
these twenty-nine minutes, no one did
make any such indication of suffering.
Mr. Wang has had both sides of this
unfortunate affair placed before him
in the columns of this paper in the
form of statements issued by the or-
ganisations concerned. A proper ap-
preciation of evidential values can only
lead to one conclusion. The original
report appearing in the North-China
Daily News has been proved to be
substantially correct.

康纳路丑闻
一些冷静的思考
致《字林西报》编辑
先生，——从贵报读者来信栏目所占篇幅来看，公众对“康纳路事件”的兴趣似乎并未减弱，反而因各种读者各站一方、互相指责而日益增加，鉴于此，我能否再次请求一点版面，恳请那些冲动的人在听取完整案情之前不要急于谴责，而是进行更多冷静的思考。
我只想提请人们注意一个关键点，该点已被忽视，因为“种族偏见”、“界外道路”以及其他涉及互相揭短的无关问题引发了如此多的热度，以至于真正的问题在迷雾中被忽视了。
作出陈述的人应准备好在被要求时证实该陈述，这是一条公理。因此，那些声称事故的不幸受害者并非当场死亡的人有责任提出他们所拥有的最有力证据来支持其主张，因为该主张已受到反驳。一旦他们的案件成立，那时才是要求公共安全局（Bureau of Public Safety）解释任何需要解释之事的时候。我并非试图为该局辩护，如果针对该局的指控全部属实，我将全心全意加入谴责行列。但我注意到，所有报告都奇怪地对官方死亡证明或验尸官调查结果保持沉默。然而，这正是整个事件的关键所在。4月13日出现在贵报栏目的公共汽车公司声明中顺便提到，“死因为休克”。众所周知，死于事故伤害的人 invariably 会在某种程度上遭受休克。然而，缺失的医学证词的关键部分是：由何种伤害导致的休克？某些伤害确实会导致即时死亡，而医学证据或许能够立即驱散围绕此案吹嘘的所有空话。
F. T. WANG.
上海，4月16日。
***受害者在大事故发生后仍存活相当长时间证据已在本报栏目发表，且证据确凿。一名目击者看到那位不幸年轻人的手臂和腿在动。负责消防队救护车的中国学员军官向肖顿先生（Mr. Shotton）呼吁：“肖顿先生，看在上帝的份上，您能不能做点什么把人弄出来，也许我们能救他的命。”另一名目击者实际上感觉到受害者的脉搏在跳动，他也在呼吸。第四名目击者看到手臂和腿在动，看到那人最终闭上眼睛并显然死亡。那是晚上9点20分，即事故发生后二十九分钟。虽然有充分理由关心受害者在这二十九分钟内是否呻吟或哀叹，但没有人做出任何此类痛苦的表示。
王先生已通过相关机构发布的声明形式，在本报栏目中了解了这起不幸事件双方的情况。对证据价值的适当评估只能得出一个结论。《字林西报》最初发表的报道已被证明大体正确。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. & S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D 57
Date ____ / ____ / 1934

CONNAUGHT RD. SCANDAL
The Facts Examined
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—I have carefully gone over the facts of the Connaught Road scandal and have also carefully read the Chinese version of the affair, and find it to be nothing more or less than a tirade against the Shanghai Municipal Police and Extrality. The evidence advanced by both members of the Bus Company and police force appears to be clear and truthful, even down to the fact that they actually have the number of the Chapel policemen who laid violent hands on one of the would-be rescuers.
If, as the Chinese version goes, a photographer was only a hundred yards down the road and that he was on the scene almost immediately, why on earth was the unfortunate victim not removed from under the bus until nearly an hour after the accident occurred. It sounds weak to me, to say the least of it.
The accusation made by the Chinese police that the face of the victim's mother was slapped by a Foreign police officer is absolutely unbelievable. I have opportunity enough of seeing our police at work and know for a fact that, whilst they are hard on law breakers, they are most kindly in their attitude towards suffers. Kinder and fairer men than Messrs. Tullock and Pridmore, who we are informed had charge of the case, could not be found. Do the Chinese police really think that any sane thinking person, Chinese or Foreign, would believe the story that men who behaved themselves as Messrs. Tullock and Pridmore did under most provoking circumstances only a few minutes before would sink to the level of striking a woman who had just lost her only son under the most tragic circumstances? I say, shame! on those who started and gave voice to so foul a charge. The Municipal Council will surely not let such a statement pass unchallenged.
The statement made by the Chinese inferring that justice cannot be obtained against persons enjoying extrality rights is an insult to every foreign court in Shanghai, and should be vigorously protested by those concerned.
In concluding, present me, Mr. Editor, to congratulate you on the stand you have taken and the energetic manner in which you have gone about getting to the truth of this shameful affair. Let us hope that your efforts on behalf of Humanity, Truth, and Justice will not be in vain.
FOR TRUTH.
Shanghai, Apr. 15.

康纳路丑闻
事实审查
致《字林西报》编辑
先生，——我已仔细审查了康纳路丑闻的事实，也仔细阅读了该事件的中文版本，发现其无非是对上海公共租界工部局警务处和治外法权的猛烈抨击。公共汽车公司成员和警察部队双方提出的证据似乎清晰且真实，甚至包括他们确实掌握了动手殴打一名试图施救者的巡捕房警察的编号这一事实。
如果按照中文版本的说法，一名摄影师就在路下一百码处，并且几乎立即到达现场，那么为什么不幸的受害者直到事故发生近一小时后才被从公共汽车下移走。这听起来至少可以说是软弱的。
中国警察指控受害者母亲的脸被一名外籍警官打了一巴掌，这绝对令人难以置信。我有足够的机会观察我们的警察工作，并确切知道，虽然他们对违法者严厉，但对受苦者态度非常和蔼。据告知负责此案的图洛克先生（Mr. Tullock）和普里德莫尔先生（Mr. Pridmore），再也找不到比他们更仁慈、更公正的人了。中国警察真的认为，任何思维健全的人，无论是中国人还是外国人，会相信这样一个故事吗：即在几分钟前在最令人恼火的情况下表现得体的图洛克先生和普里德莫尔先生，会在最悲惨的情况下刚刚失去独子的妇女面前堕落到殴打她的地步？我说，羞耻！献给那些发起并宣扬如此污蔑指控的人。工部局肯定不会让这样的陈述未经挑战就通过。
中国人所作的暗示，即无法对享有治外法权权利的人获得正义，这是对上海每个外国法庭的侮辱，应由有关方面强烈抗议。
最后，编辑先生，请允许我祝贺您所采取的立场以及您为查明这起可耻事件真相所付出的精力充沛的方式。让我们希望您为人性、真理和正义所做的努力不会白费。
为了真理。
上海，4月15日。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Saturday, April 14, 1934    8948

AS A CHINESE SEES IT
THE CONNAUGHT ROAD ACCIDENT
By KWEI CHUNG-SHU

HUMAN credulity was taxed to the full during the European war when German atrocities were depicted with all vividness. It was not until ten years after the Armistice that the world, thanks to independent historians, began to appreciate the other side of the story. The propaganda machinery of the Allies proved so efficient that some of its surviving manipulators have never lost an opportunity to pride themselves reminiscently on their ingenuity.

Shanghai seems to be passing through a miniature world war ever since the Connaught Road incident occurred last Saturday. Chinese life in this community has seldom appeared so precious to a certain contemporary as it has in the present case. So much of its valuable front-page space has been devoted to the cause of humanity and truth that one is almost inclined to believe that the outrages committed by the Japanese against the Chinese in Hongkew in 1932, judged by the meagre accounts given by the same journal, must be read like mere bedtime stories.

How It Started
THE incident arose from a traffic accident in which a bus ran over a Chinese cyclist. The bus company and the municipal police claim that the Chinese police had prevented the removal of the victim from underneath the bus till a photograph was taken of the scene.

Many details have been drawn into this controversy, but only a few need be taken seriously into account. The main issue centers around the condition of the victim immediately after the accident. The bus company's officials and the municipal police are positive that the cyclist knocked down did not die till he was removed to the ambulance after a photograph had been taken, and that his life might have been saved had immediate medical aid been rendered.

For the Chinese police it is stated that the victim died instantly after the accident and that there appeared no sign of life to give hope for resuscitation.

The question is when a man is to be proclaimed dead. On this point is to be found many a theory of medico jurisprudence, but according to the Chinese law which, I presume, is to govern the case at issue, a man is dead when visible breathing has stopped. On this basis it is obviously within the competence of a police officer or any normal-minded person, to ascertain the extinction of life.

A Common Sense View
**〔此处转录不清〕**

In fact, their action in trying to save a human being over the alleged unwarranted attitude of the recalcitrant Chinese police would have been upheld by Chinese law, and one wonders why these humanitarian brothers of mercy hesitated to combat force with force but chose to submit as tame lambs while the victim was being slowly reduced to death! If the Chinese police were guilty of commission then they would be guilty of omission.

The Root Of The Agitation
THE apparent tendency to make a mountain of a mole hill is of course engendered by no humanitarian motive. It is singular for instance, that so much has been written about the cruelty of the Chinese police and nothing has yet been said about the culpable negligence of the bus driver involved. While the attempt to divert the issue may provide an excuse for the driver to avoid a charge of manslaughter and the company to evade civil damages, this controversy is really an incident in the larger question of extra-settlement roads. If the incident had happened where the settlement would a hue and cry have been raised? Therein lies the clue to the whole agitation.

Unfortunately, however, the solution to this time-honored problem is not to be evolved through a series of futile provocative controversies. The Chinese have always maintained a friendly attitude throughout the negotiations, and the only obstacles have been placed by the Japanese and not the Chinese. If this fact is faced frankly, considerable aid may be saved. It is more practicable to follow the suggestion of Mr. O. S. Franklin and Mr. F. E. Harris, to adopt stronger measures toward the Chinese than resort to underhand tactics. That example, by virtue of force at the command of the colonial body, has shown what it wants. But such a course is fraught with danger.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE

华人视角
康纳路事故
作者：桂中枢（KWEI CHUNG-SHU，音译）

在欧洲大战期间，当德国的暴行被描绘得栩栩如生时，人类的轻信受到了极大的考验。直到停战十年后，世界才得益于独立历史学家的研究，开始了解到故事的另一面。协约国的宣传机器证明是如此高效，以至于其一些幸存的操纵者从未失去机会，带着回忆自豪地夸耀他们的巧思。

自从上周六康纳路事故发生以来，上海似乎正经历着一场微型的世界大战。在这个社区中，中国人的生命在当代某些人眼中，从未像在当前这一案例中显得如此珍贵。该报将如此多宝贵的头版篇幅 devoted to 人道与真理的事业，以至于人们几乎倾向于相信，根据同一份报纸所给出的寥寥数语的报道来判断，1932年日本人在虹口对中国人犯下的暴行，读起来必定就像单纯的睡前故事一般。

起因
此次事件源于一桩交通事故，一辆公共汽车轧过了一名中国骑自行车的人。公共汽车公司和工部局警务处声称，中国警察阻止了在拍摄现场照片之前将受害者从车下移走。

许多细节被卷入这场争议，但只有少数几点需要认真考量。主要问题集中在事故发生后受害者的状况。公共汽车公司的官员和工部局警务处坚称，被撞倒的骑车人在拍照后被移至救护车前并未死亡，如果立即给予医疗救助，他的生命或许可以得救。

据称，对于中国警察而言，受害者在事故后立即死亡，且没有任何生命迹象表明有复苏的希望。

问题在于何时宣布一个人死亡。在此问题上可以找到许多法医学理论，但根据我认为应管辖此案的中國法律，当可见的呼吸停止时，人即被视为死亡。在此基础上，警官或任何心智正常的人显然有能力确定生命的终结。

常识观点
**〔此处转录不清〕**

事实上，他们试图拯救人类的行为，针对的是所谓顽固的中国警察的不当态度，这本应得到中国法律的支持；人们不禁要问，这些仁慈的人道主义兄弟为何犹豫不决，不以力抗力，却在受害者慢慢走向死亡时选择像温顺的羔羊一样屈服！如果中国警察犯了作为之罪，那么他们也就犯了不作为之罪。

骚动的根源
这种显然倾向于小题大做的做法，当然不是由任何人道主义动机产生的。例如，奇怪的是，关于中国警察残酷性的文章写得如此之多，而对于涉事公共汽车司机的可谴责的疏忽却只字未提。虽然试图转移议题可能为司机避免过失杀人指控以及为公司逃避民事赔偿提供借口，但这场争议实际上是租界外道路这一更大问题中的一个插曲。如果事件发生在租界内，是否会引发同样的强烈抗议？这正是整个骚动的线索所在。

然而不幸的是，这一历史悠久的问题的解决方案，并非通过一系列徒劳且具挑衅性的争议所能达成。中国人在整个谈判过程中始终保持友好态度，唯一的障碍是由日本人而非中国人设置的。如果坦率面对这一事实，或许能节省大量的援助。遵循 O. S. Franklin 先生和 F. E. Harris 先生的建议，对中国采取更强硬的措施，比诉诸暗中手段更为可行。那个例子凭借殖民机构所掌握的武力，展示了其想要什么。但这样的过程充满危险。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, APRIL 14, 1934
8544

Bus Company Makes Report
On Tragic Incident

Statements From Foreign Officials Actually At
Scene Of Accident On Connaught Road;
Police Officer Pushed Over

In connection with the accident
on Connaught Road last Satur-
day evening, resulting in the
death of a Chinese cyclist who
was pinned beneath one of the
buses of the China General
Omnibus Company and whose body
was prevented from being removed
by police of the Public Safety
Bureau, the Bus Company has
issued the following statement:

In view of the contradictory
reports that have appeared in
various local papers regarding
the bus accident which was fol-
lowed by a fatal result on the
evening of Saturday last, and of
the action of the Public Safety
Bureau in constables or other offi-
cers in connection therewith, it
is felt that the following evidence
from members of the staff of this
Company is pertinent.

The accident occurred at 6.07
p.m. and 56 minutes elapsed be-
fore the ambulance removed the
victim who by then had expired.
The Chief Engineer and Traffic
Manager of the Company, who
lives in the vicinity, was himself
a witness of most of what occur-
red, while three British members
of the staff were also witnesses.
Your reports of the occurrence,
to date, have perhaps overstress-
ed the shrieks of agony, but
there is evidence that the unfor-
tunate victim was alive for some
time after the accident, and that
he did utter sounds of suffering.

Cyclist Pinned Beneath

The bus ran over a cyclist who
cut across in front of it in Con-
naught Road, near the Bus Depot.
The cyclist was pinned under the
front part of the bus with his
machine.

Mr. Malleck, a British foreman
employed in the Bus Company's
garage, was one of the first on
the scene. He saw the legs and
arms of the cyclist moving, and
was sure that he was alive. Then
he and a Chinese garage hand
endeavoured to lift the bus by
means of breakdown jacks. They
lifted it a few inches, and were
prevented from further work by
constables of the Public Safety
Bureau.

A Shanghai Fire Brigade am-
bulance arrived in charge of a
Chinese Officer Cadet of the
Brigade, who finding that the
Chapei Police would not allow
the removal of the casualty, sent
one of his crew with Mr. Malleck
by car to telephone to Gordon
Road Police Station for assistance.

Later the Cadet appealed to
Mr. J. D. E. Shotter, Chief Eng-
ineer and Traffic Manager of the
Company, saying "Mr. Shotter
for God's sake get out and do
something." Mr. Shotter went out
and found the situation as de-
scribed.

Police Take Over

As the Settlement Police from
Gordon Road had by that time
arrived, under the command of
Sub-Inspectors Tulloch and Prid-
more, Mr. Shotter replied that he
had handed the matter over to
them.

Mr. Malleck saw Mr. Alfred
Huxley, Night Superintendent of
the Company, attempt to pull the
cyclist from under the bus; he
also saw a Chapei constable pre-
venting him from doing so, by pull-
ing Mr. Huxley away, at the
same time threatening Mr. Huxley
by placing his hand on his pistol
holster.

Officer Pushed Over

Mr. Malleck saw Sub-Inspector
Pridmore pushed over a stretcher
by the Chapei Police, Mr. Prid-
more falling to the ground. He
also saw the Settlement officer in
plain-clothes (Sub-Inspector Tul-
loch) pushed by the Chapei Police.

Mr. Huxley received the in-
formation regarding the accident
a few minutes after it occurred,
and at once proceeded to the
scene. He found the cyclist alive,
he was breathing and his pulse
was beating. Mr. Huxley gave
orders for the jack to be used,
but Constables of the Public
Safety Bureau refused to allow
this. Mr. Huxley then forced his
way through the large crowd
round the bus, and told Mr.
Malleck to use the jack, which he
did, the bus being lifted a few
inches.

Mr. Huxley bent down and at-
tempted to pull the cyclist out,
but he was seized by Constable
**〔此处转录不清〕** of the Public Safety
Bureau, pulled backward and thus
prevented from lifting out the
cyclist. The same constable sub-
sequently snatched Mr. Huxley's
flashlight from him, for the use
of the photograph.

Officer Knocked Down

The crowd was continually in-
creasing, and Mr. Huxley asked
Sub-Inspectors Tulloch and Prid-
more to keep it back. Sub-In-
spector Pridmore attempted to
do so, but was knocked down by
the Chapei Police. A message
was sent to Gordon Road Police
Station asking for reinforcements
which arrived later in two cars.

After their arrival a photo-
graph was taken by a Chinese
photographer following which the
cyclist was removed from under
the bus, but on removal appeared
to be dead.

Mr. R. A. Taylor, Traffic In-
spector of the Bus Company, first
heard of the accident while on
duty on the Company's premises
and telephoned for the ambulance.

Still Alive

His evidence is that on arrival
at the scene of the accident a few
minutes after its occurrence he
saw the arms and legs of the
cyclist moving. He states that
the casualty was alive until 6.36
p.m. at which time he saw the
eyes close. This was 29 minutes
after the accident occurred.

At 7.03 p.m. the body was re-
moved from under the bus and
placed on an ambulance which
left at once for the Chinese Red
Cross Hospital in Avenue Haig.
On arrival there at 7.14 p.m. the
man was found to be dead, and
subsequently a death certificate
was issued giving the cause of
death as shock.

Statements have been put for-
ward by sundry persons to the
effect that the cyclist expired al-
most immediately after the ac-
cident—whether they are competent
to judge is another matter—but
from the above evidence it is
clear that he survived for some
time. Had early medical atten-
tion been made available his life
might have been saved or at
least his sufferings mitigated.

It cannot be emphasized too
strongly that in the common in-
terests of humanity the victim
of any accident should be render-
ed the earliest possible medical
attention, it being presumed that
he is alive until life is pronounc-
ed extinct by competent authority.

There can be no doubt that the
efforts of the Shanghai Municipal
Police, the Fire Department, Am-
bulance Service and the Bus Com-
pany's employees to succour the
injured party were frustrated by
the members of the Bureau of
Public Safety.

公共汽车公司就悲剧事件提交报告

来自康纳路事故现场的外国官员的陈述；
一名警官被推倒

关于上周六晚上在康纳路发生的事故，该事故导致一名中国骑自行车的人死亡，他被压在上海公共汽车公司（China General Omnibus Company）的一辆公共汽车下，且其遗体被公安局警察阻止移走，公共汽车公司发布了以下声明：

鉴于当地各报纸就上周六晚上造成致命后果的公共汽车事故出现了相互矛盾的报道，以及公安局巡捕或其他官员在此事中的行动，本公司认为以下来自本公司员工的证据是相关的。

事故发生在下午6:07，在救护车移走受害者之前经过了56分钟，此时受害者已身亡。居住在该附近的本公司总工程师兼交通经理亲自目睹了大部分发生的情况，另有三名英籍员工也是目击者。截至目前，贵报对事件的报道或许过分强调了痛苦的尖叫，但有证据表明，不幸的受害者在事故后存活了一段时间，并且确实发出了痛苦的声音。

骑车人被压在车下

公共汽车在康纳路靠近车场处，轧过了一名从车前横穿马路的骑车人。骑车人连人带车被压在公共汽车的前部下方。

受雇于公共汽车公司车库的英籍领班 Malleck 先生是最早到达现场的人员之一。他看到骑车人的手脚在动，确信他还活着。随后，他和一名中国车库工人试图利用急救千斤顶抬起公共汽车。他们将车抬起了几英寸，但被公安局的巡捕阻止继续工作。

上海消防队的一辆救护车抵达，由消防队的一名中国见习官负责指挥。他发现闸北警察不允许移走伤者，便派出一名队员随 Malleck 先生乘车前往戈登路警察局求助。

随后，该见习官向公司总工程师兼交通经理 J. D. E. Shotter 先生呼吁说：“Shotter 先生，看在上帝的份上，出去做点什么吧。” Shotter 先生走出去，发现情况正如所述。

警方接管

由于此时来自戈登路的租界警察已在副督察 Tulloch 和 Pridmore 的指挥下抵达，Shotter 先生回答说，他已将此事移交给他们。

Malleck 先生看到公司夜间主管 Alfred Huxley 先生试图将骑车人从车下拉出；他还看到一名闸北巡捕通过将 Huxley 先生拉开来阻止他这样做，同时把手放在枪套上威胁 Huxley 先生。

警官被推倒

Malleck 先生看到副督察 Pridmore 被闸北警察推过一副担架，Pridmore 先生摔倒在地。他还看到便衣租界警官（副督察 Tulloch）被闸北警察推搡。

Huxley 先生在事故发生几分钟后收到有关事故的信息，并立即前往现场。他发现骑车人还活着，正在呼吸，脉搏也在跳动。Huxley 先生下令使用千斤顶，但公安局巡捕拒绝允许。随后，Huxley 先生强行穿过包围公共汽车的人群，告诉 Malleck 先生使用千斤顶，Malleck 照做了，公共汽车被抬起了几英寸。

Huxley 先生弯下腰，试图将骑车人拉出来，但他被公安局的一名巡捕 **〔此处转录不清〕** 抓住，向后拉扯，从而无法将骑车人拉出。同一名巡捕随后夺走了 Huxley 先生的手电筒，用于拍照。

警官被撞倒

人群不断增加，Huxley 先生请求副督察 Tulloch 和 Pridmore 驱散人群。副督察 Pridmore 试图这样做，但被闸北警察撞倒。有人向戈登路警察局发送消息请求增援，增援人员随后乘坐两辆汽车抵达。

在他们抵达后，一名中国摄影师拍摄了一张照片，随后骑车人被从车下移出，但在移出时似乎已经死亡。

公共汽车公司的交通稽查员 R. A. Taylor 先生在公司场所值班时首次听说事故，并打电话呼叫救护车。

仍然活着

他的证词是，在事故发生几分钟后到达现场时，他看到骑车人的手脚在动。他陈述说，伤者一直活到下午6:36，当时他看到死者闭上了眼睛。这是事故发生后29分钟。

下午7:03，遗体从车下移出并放置在一辆救护车上，该车立即前往海格路（Avenue Haig）的中国红十字会医院。下午7:14到达那里时，发现此人已死亡，随后签发了死亡证明，死因为休克。

各色人等提出的说法声称，骑车人在事故后几乎立即死亡——他们是否有能力判断是另一回事——但从上述证据来看，显然他存活了一段时间。如果能尽早获得医疗关注，他的生命或许可以得救，或者至少减轻他的痛苦。

必须极力强调，出于人道的共同利益，任何事故的受害者都应尽快获得医疗救助，假定其在有权限当局宣布生命终结之前仍然活着。

毫无疑问，上海公共租界工部局警务处、消防处、救护车服务处以及公共汽车公司员工为救助伤者所做的努力，遭到了公安局成员的阻挠。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, FRIDAY, APRIL 13, 1934.

BUS ACCIDENT
A Chinese Reader's Letter
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—Will you be so good as to allow a Chinese reader to express a little comment on the Connaught Road "incident." I know as much about the matter as your other correspondents—nothing more than I have read in the newspapers, and as conflicting reports have appeared I am just as bewildered as ever as to what actually took place.
My object in writing this letter is to suggest that before your readers allow themselves to be carried away by indignation at the "inhuman" conduct of the Chinese police that they wait until the actual facts have been established.
Meanwhile, although I know that "two blacks don't make a white," I would like to mention that a recent visitor to Hongkong, Canon H. W. Brady, C.B.E., in the course of an interview told the reporters of an incident which occurred during his residence in South America. He was sent to prison for striking a policeman, after rescuing a girl from drowning.
"I got her out of the water, laid her on the ground and as she appeared to be all in I tried artificial respiration until help arrived. The 'help' arrived in the shape of the police, one of whom promptly hit me over the head with a chain. I went for the fellow and the next thing I remember was waking up in a cell.
"There is a curious law there that, in such a case as this, the person who has been injured or endangered must not be touched until the police or doctor arrives. Even if a person is run over by a car, he must be left entirely alone, though the doctor may not arrive for an hour or two."
I do not know what instructions have been issued by the Chinese police authorities, but I do think some of your correspondents should refrain from abuse until the facts of the Connaught Road "Incident" have been clearly established. Then it will be time to place the blame—and even then it should be possible to do so without using expressions which are offensive, and are apparently intended to be. I can assure you that some of us are just as anxious as foreigners that things in this country should be done in accordance with the highest accepted standards of modern civilisation, but we do not expect judgments to be formed while facts are still in dispute.
F. T. WANG.
Shanghai, Apr. 12.
***Mr. Wang will be better able to appreciate the truth of the original story after perusal of the eye-witnesses' accounts of what actually took place on Saturday evening. He is to be congratulated upon the very moderate tone of his letter, but he will surely realise that the deep indignation which is demonstrated has been aroused over the fate of one of his own countrymen.

《字林西报》，1934年4月13日，星期五。

公共汽车事故
一位中国读者的来信
致《字林西报》编辑先生：

先生，能否请您允许一位中国读者就康纳路（Connaught Road）“事件”发表一点评论？我对这件事的了解程度与贵报其他通讯员一样——除了我在报纸上读到的内容外，一无所知；由于报道相互矛盾，我对实际发生的情况同样感到困惑。

我写这封信的目的是建议，在读者们因中国警察的“不人道”行为而义愤填膺之前，应等待事实真相查明。

与此同时，虽然我知道“两个错误加在一起并不等于正确”，但我愿提及最近访问香港的 H. W. Brady 教士（C.B.E.勋衔）。他在接受采访时向记者讲述了一件他在南美洲居住期间发生的事件。他因从水中救出一名女孩后殴打了一名警察而被送进监狱。

“我把她从水里救出来，放在地上，因为她看起来已经奄奄一息，我便对她进行人工呼吸，直到救援到来。‘救援’是以警察的形式到来的，其中一人立即用链条猛击我的头部。我冲向那个家伙，接下来我记得的就是在牢房里醒来了。

“那里有一条奇怪的法律，规定在这种情况下，在警察或医生到达之前，不得触碰受伤或处于危险中的人。即使有人被汽车撞倒，也必须让他完全独自待着，尽管医生可能要过一两个小时才能到达。”

我不知道中国警方当局发布了什么指令，但我认为，在康纳路“事件”的事实清楚确立之前，贵报的一些通讯员应避免谩骂。那时才是追究责任的时候——即便到那时，也应该能够不使用那些具有冒犯性、且显然意在冒犯的措辞来追究责任。我可以向你们保证，我们中的一些人和外国人一样，迫切希望这个国家的事情能按照现代文明公认的最高标准来处理，但我们不期望在事实仍有争议时就做出评判。

F. T. WANG.
上海，4月12日。
***王先生在仔细阅读了关于周六晚上实际发生情况的目击者陈述后，将能更好地领会原始故事的真实性。他的信件语气非常温和，值得称赞，但他肯定会意识到，所表现出的强烈义愤是由他的一位同胞的遭遇所激起的。

Min Pao and other local newspapers :

ANNIVERSARY OF KUOMINTANG PURIFICATION MOVEMENT

Yesterday being the Anniversary of the Purification Movement of the Kuomintang, the Shanghai District Kuomintang Headquarters held a commemoration meeting at 10 a.m. Some 200 persons representing various circles were present. Precautionary measures were adopted both in the Chinese controlled territory and the Settlements. However no untoward incidents occurred during the day.

Sin Wan Pao (Tokyo Telegram):

RESTORATION OF JAPANESE SETTLEMENTS DENIED.

The Japanese Foreign Ministry states that no official despatch concerning the restoration of the Japanese concessions at Soochow and Hangchow has been received. The statement adds that all questions between China and Japan must be settled before the concessions are restored.

Sin Wan Pao (Nanking Telegram):

BRITAIN'S MILITARY STRENGTH AT HONGKONG.

According to information secured from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the British Government, in view of the tense situation in the Far East, has increased the military strength at Hongkong.

China Times and other local newspapers:

BUS ACCIDENT ON CONNAUGHT ROAD

With reference to the death of a Chinese named Sun, who was knocked down by a bus belonging to the China General Omnibus Company, reports have appeared in the newspapers, but it is ascertained that some of the points mentioned in those reports are not accurate;
The home of the deceased is in the vicinity of the scene of the accident. At about 6 p.m. on the date of the accident, the deceased left home on a bicycle. He went along Connaught Road from west to east. He was following a bus of the China General Omnibus Company, when he was suddenly knocked down by the rear wheel of the bus on the road between houses Nos. 373 and 375. At this juncture, Bus No. 15007 dashed along from east to west. The driver of the bus took no notice of the injured man on the road. When his car came near the man, he applied the brake, the bus passing over the man. Death was instantaneous. When the driver saw that an accident occurred, he fled at once. There was a crowd of spectators.
Informed of the accident, the mother of the deceased, Sun Owng Sze, came immediately to the scene. After finding that the body of her son was cold, she burst into tears.

国民党清党运动周年纪念

昨日为国民党清党运动周年纪念日，上海市党部于上午10时举行纪念大会。各界代表约200人出席。在华界及租界均采取了预防措施。然而，当日未发生任何意外事件。

否认恢复日本租界。

日本外务省声明，未收到关于恢复苏州和杭州日本租界的官方照会。该声明补充说，中日之间所有问题必须在恢复租界之前得到解决。

英国在香港的军事力量。

《时报》及其他本地报纸：

康纳路公共汽车事故

关于一名姓孙的中国人被英商中国公共汽车公司（China General Omnibus Company）所属公共汽车撞死一事，报纸上已有报道，但经查明，这些报道中提到的某些要点并不准确；

死者住所位于事故现场附近。事故发生当日傍晚6时许，死者骑自行车离家。他沿康纳路由西向东行驶。当他跟随一辆中国公共汽车公司的公共汽车行驶时，在373号和375号房屋之间的路段，突然被该公共汽车的后轮撞倒。此时，15007号公共汽车由东向西疾驰而来。该车司机对路上的伤者未予理会。当车靠近此人时，他踩下刹车，公共汽车从此人身上碾过。死者当场死亡。司机见发生事故，随即逃逸。现场有一群围观者。

死者母亲孙翁氏（Sun Owng Sze）获悉事故后，立即赶到现场。发现儿子身体已冷，不禁痛哭失声。

April 13, 1934.    Morning Translation.

As the place of the accident is an extra-Settlement
road, Chinese Police came immediately to the scene.
Finding that the man had been killed, they sent for a
photographer to take a photograph of the scene to be used
as evidence in case a dispute should arise.
When Settlement Police arrived and found that the
Chinese Police were there before them, they were dissatis-
fied. Seeing that the driver of one of the buses had
already escaped, they thought that large compensation
might be demanded and complained that the man was only
injured and that he died in consequence of the delay
necessitated by the taking of a photograph.
Yesterday the Settlement Police authorities sent
a protest to the Bureau of Public Safety with a view to
evading the responsibility for the death on behalf of
the China General Omnibus Company and the driver of the
bus.
It is learned that the relatives of the deceased
have retained the services of a lawyer and will file a
charge against the company.
It is also indicated that the China General Omnibus
Company sent representatives yesterday and the day before
yesterday to discuss the question of compensation with
the relatives of the deceased in order to settle the matter,
but that the family had found out that the driver was once
involved in an accident for which he was imprisoned for
eight months and that he was released from prison only
three days ago. The family refused to settle the matter
with the Company and insisted on charging the driver in
order that he might be suitably punished for his negligence.
Following the accident, the residents have paid
much attention to the development of the case and if
necessary a mass meeting of the residents will be held.

April 12, 1934.                                      Lorning Translation.

Central China Daily News, Shun Pao and other local newspapers:

BUS ACCIDENT ON CONNAUGHT ROAD.

    According to reports published on April 10 in
the "North China Daily News", a local foreign newspaper,
a bus belonging to the China General Omnibus Company,
a British concern, at 6 p.m. April 7 knocked down a Ghinese
on Connaught Road (extra-Settlement road) and the victim
died because the Chinese policeman desired to take a
photo of the victim and did not allow the victim to be
immediately rushed to hospital for treatment.
    Interviewed yesterday by our reporter, Colonel
Tan Pao-zeu (葆壽), officer-in-charge of the 6th
Division Police made the following statement:-
    "At 6.07 p.m. April 7, when a bus, Route 10, of
the China General Omnibus Company was being driven from
west to east on Connaught Road, the deceased, Sung Hoong-
chwang (沈鴻章), son of the proprietor of a cigarette
shop at No. 360 Connaught Road, was riding a bicycle in
the same direction on the right side of the bus. Meantime,
another bus, Route 10, (No. 15007) of the same concern
was proceeding from east to west and in order to allow
the bus to pass, Sung Hoong-chwang rode to the left side
and was knocked down by the back wheel of the right side
of the bus running from west to east and the right front
wheel of the bus (No. 15007) crushed his neck and chest.
    "Upon learning of this, the post duty policeman
concerned went to the scene and the bus driver No. 407
had already left the scene. Sung Hoong-chwang died
instantaneously of serious wounds. The death could be
testified by his mother Sung Cong-tz (沈翁氏) and one
witness named Moh Wen-tuh (馬文德) who clearly saw that
the body of the victim was motionless.
    "In view of the fact that the victim had already
died, this District Police had to take a photo of the
deceased but the Gordon Road Station desired to remove
the dead body. The report published by the "North China
Daily News" to the effect that the wounded man met his
death because the Chinese policeman did not allow him to
be sent to hospital at once is absolutely contrary to fact.
Such reports evidently show that those who are concerned
intend to evade the responsibility for the accident."

《华中日报》、《申报》及其他本地报纸：

康纳路公共汽车事故。

    据4月10日本地外文报纸《字林西报》刊登的报道，4月7日下午6时，英商中国公共汽车公司所属的一辆公共汽车在康纳路（租界外道路）撞倒一名中国人，受害者因中国警察要求对受害者拍照而不允许立即将其送往医院救治而死亡。
    本报记者昨日采访了第六区警察主管谭宝寿（Tan Pao-zeu，音译，原文注：葆壽）上校，他发表如下声明：
    “4月7日下午6时07分，当中国公共汽车公司10路公共汽车沿康纳路由西向东行驶时，死者沈鸿章（Sung Hoong-chwang，音译），系康纳路360号一家烟纸店店主之子，正骑着自行车在该公共汽车右侧同向行驶。与此同时，该公司另一辆10路公共汽车（15007号）由东向西行驶，为了让该车通过，沈鸿章骑向左侧，被由西向东行驶的公共汽车右侧后轮撞倒，随后15007号公共汽车的右前轮碾过其颈部和胸部。
    “得知此事后，相关值班警察赶赴现场，而407号公共汽车司机已离开现场。沈鸿章因重伤当场死亡。其母沈翁氏（Sung Cong-tz，音译）及一名名为马文德（Moh Wen-tuh，音译）的目击者可作证，后者清楚地看到受害者身体已不动弹。
    “鉴于受害者已经死亡，本区警察不得不为死者拍照，但戈登路捕房希望移走尸体。《字林西报》发布的报道声称伤者因中国警察不允许立即送医而死亡，这完全与事实不符。此类报道显然表明，有关方面意图逃避事故责任。”

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, APRIL 12, 1934.
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. S. & S. F. REGISTRY.
No. D 5791
Date 12 / 4 / 34

Chinese Authorities Reply
To Accident Report

Denial Of Statement That Victim Of 'Bus Accident
On Connaught Road Was Not Killed Instantly;
Official Statement From Officials

The following official statement regarding the tragic accident on Connaught Road last Saturday, in which a Chinese was killed after being knocked down by an omnibus, has been forwarded to "The Shanghai Times" for publication by the City Government of Greater Shanghai, through the secretary, Mr. T. Y. Chang. The statement is published as received:

"In connection with the Connaught Road Incident in which a Chinese riding a bicycle was knocked down and killed by a 'bus of the China Omnibus Co., Ltd., the following statement has been issued by the City Government of Greater Shanghai:

"Thorough investigation and questioning of eye-witnesses of the accident have revealed the following facts:—

"1.—Shortly after six o'clock, last Saturday afternoon, April 7, two 'buses with passengers were travelling along Connaught Road in opposite directions. A Chinese riding a bicycle was travelling side by side with the east-bound 'bus when another 'bus, Settlement licence No. 15007, came along from the opposite direction. The cycle hit the right rear wheel of the first 'bus, and was thrown over with its rider. 'Bus 15007, coming from the east, did not or was unable to pull to a stop. Its right front wheel rolled over the chest and neck of the fallen man, dragging him and his bicycle along for a little distance.

"2.—Up to this point all reports seem to agree, but from this point on reports appearing in the foreign press differ from the finding of Chinese investigation in that while the former state that the victim died nearly an hour after, the latter shows that the man was killed instantly. According to a report issued to the 'North China Daily News' and other foreign dailies, the man was 'shrieking from pain' even after the arrival of the Settlement ambulance. According to a woman eye-witness, who was going in the same direction and saw the whole occurrence, the man was killed instantly and no shrieking or groaning was heard. This is corroborated by the man's own mother, who lives but 50 feet away from the scene of the accident, and was among the first to arrive on the spot. She is positive that her son did not show any sign of life still less any noise. This was before the arrival of the ambulance or even of the party of 'Bus Company's workers, who a few minutes later began to jack up the car. Just imagine the mother of the man making no protest while her son was pinned under the car and was shrieking from pain. Only a person absolutely out of his senses would believe such a story.

"3.—When the ambulance arrived, the car had already been jacked up. It was then that the ambulance men proceeded to remove the dead, not dying, man. The Chinese police held, however, that the corpse should not be removed until a photographic record of the accident had been obtained. This was done.

"4.—Again, the press reports would have us believe that it took nearly half an hour for the Chinese police to secure a photographer from Bubbling Well Road. The fact, however, is that the photographer was only about 100 yards away, he having been sent for immediately after the accident occurred. He arrived within five minutes and took the necessary photographs.

"5.—The mother of the victim states that she was taken to the Gordon Road station and kept there until nearly midnight, when she was told to appear the following morning to be taken to the mortuary. When she protested against the illegal detention and cried out aloud over the death of her only son, a foreign officer slapped her face and told her to "shut up."

"6.—The next morning, the mother called at the Gordon Road station, bringing with her a woman eye-witness. This important witness was not permitted to appear before the Chinese Coroner.

"The City Government of Greater Shanghai emphasizes that it was the removal of the dead body, but not that of a dying man that was objected to by the Chinese police, whose duty naturally it was to obtain as complete evidence as possible. This is all the more necessary in view of the great difficulty to obtain redress against those enjoying extraterritorial rights, whose reckless driving on Chinese highways has been responsible for so many tragic accidents. The City Government therefore deplores the deliberate distortion of facts as appearing in the press."

中国当局就事故报告作出回复

否认关于康纳路（Connaught Road）公交车事故受害者并非当场死亡的说法；
官员发表正式声明

大上海市政府通过秘书张廷扬（T. Y. Chang，音译）先生，向《字林西报》 forwarded 了以下关于上周六康纳路悲剧性事故的正式声明，该事故中一名华人被一辆公共汽车撞倒后身亡。该声明按收到原文刊登如下：

“关于康纳路事件，即一名骑自行车的华人被中华公共汽车股份有限公司（China Omnibus Co., Ltd.）的一辆公共汽车撞倒并致死一事，大上海市政府发表如下声明：

“通过对事故的彻底调查及对目击者的讯问，查明事实如下：—

“1.—上周六下午，即4月7日，六点钟刚过，两辆载有乘客的公共汽车沿康纳路相向行驶。一名骑自行车的华人与向东行驶的公共汽车并行时，另一辆车牌号为租界执照第15007号的公共汽车从相反方向驶来。自行车撞上了第一辆公共汽车的右后轮，连人带车翻倒。从东面驶来的15007号公共汽车没有或无法停下。其右前轮碾过倒地男子的胸部和颈部，并将他和他的自行车拖行了一小段距离。

“2.—至此为止，所有报道似乎一致，但此后外文报刊的报道与中国方面的调查结果存在分歧，前者称受害者在近一小时后死亡，而后者显示该男子当场死亡。据发给《字林西报》及其他外文日报的一份报告称，即使在租界救护车到达后，该男子仍‘痛苦地尖叫’。据一位同向行驶并目睹全过程的女性目击者称，该男子当场死亡，未听到任何尖叫或呻吟声。这一点得到了死者母亲的佐证，她住在离事故现场仅50英尺的地方，是最早到达现场的人之一。她确信她的儿子没有任何生命迹象，更不用说发出声音了。这发生在救护车到达之前，甚至早于几分钟后开始用千斤顶抬起车辆的公共汽车公司工人团队到达之前。试想一下，如果她的儿子被压在车下并因痛苦而尖叫，这位母亲竟不提出抗议。只有完全丧失理智的人才会相信这样的故事。

“3.—当救护车到达时，车辆已经被千斤顶抬起。此时，救护人员才着手移走这名已死、而非垂死的男子。然而，中国警方坚持认为，在对事故进行拍照记录之前，不应移走尸体。随后完成了拍照。

“4.—此外，新闻报道试图让我们相信，中国警方花了近半个小时才从静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）请来一名摄影师。然而事实是，摄影师就在约100码之外，他在事故发生后立即被召请。他在五分钟内到达并拍摄了必要的照片。

“5.—受害者的母亲声称，她被带到戈登路（Gordon Road）巡捕房，并被扣留至接近午夜，当时被告知次日早晨出现场以便前往停尸房。当她抗议非法拘留并为其独子之死大声哭喊时，一名外籍警官打了她一记耳光，并叫她‘闭嘴’。

“6.—第二天早晨，这位母亲带着一名女性目击者来到戈登路巡捕房。这位重要的证人未被允许在中国验尸官面前作证。

“大上海市政府强调，中国警方反对的是移走死者尸体，而非移走垂死之人，警方的职责自然是尽可能获取完整的证据。鉴于向享有治外法权者寻求赔偿极为困难，而这些人在中国公路上鲁莽驾驶已导致如此多的悲剧性事故，此举显得尤为必要。因此，大上海市政府对新闻界故意歪曲事实表示痛惜。”

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, APRIL 12, 1934

Last Saturday's Incident
In Connaught Road

How Chapei Policemen Callously Prevented S.M.C.
Police Officers From Succouring Grievously
Injured Man; The Official Report

The following is the official version of the Connaught Road affair last Saturday evening, which has attracted such wide attention, issued by the Press Information Office of the Shanghai Municipal Council:

The report of the Commissioner of Police, S.M.P. to the Council states that at 6.30 p.m.. on April 7 a telephone message was received at Gordon Road Police Station from the China General Omnibus Company's Depot on Connaught Road that an accident had occurred on Connaught Road near the Depot and that Chapei Police were present and refused to allow the Fire Brigade Ambulance men and Omnibus Company officials to remove an injured person from underneath a bus. Sub-Inspector Tulloch and Sub-Inspector Pridmore at once went to the scene, where there was a large crowd of Chinese including about 15 Chapei policemen, round a bus. The S. M. Police officers were informed that the Chapei policemen had refused to permit the ambulance men and Bus Co, officials to remove from underneath the bus the injured person who, at the time they attempted to remove him, was still alive.

Chapei Police Intervene

Although Sub-Inspector Tulloch when he arrived formed the opinion that the man was dead, he gave instructions to the ambulance men to remove the man at once and convey him to hospital. Upon this the Chapei policemen intervened and prevented the removal of the man. Steps had been taken to jack up the bus to take the weight off the man, who the two Sub-Inspectors tried in vain to remove in spite of the Chapei policemen's action. The Chapei policemen, declaring that they had as much right on the road as the Settlement Police, insisted that the body should not be moved until they had received orders from their officer in charge of the Division, and also that a photograph should first be taken.

Hands On Pistols

By this time more Chapei policemen had arrived and a serious clash threatened between the Chapei Police and the Settlement Police. In order to avert a clash and to get the injured man removed, Sub-Inspector Tulloch gave orders for a photograph to be taken. The photograph was taken at 6.58 p.m. and another attempt was made to remove the man, but the Chapei policemen, in a high pitch of excitement, pushed the Settlement police and a number of them had their hands on their pistols in a threatening manner. Information was then received that the officer in charge of the Chapei Police Division had ordered his men to cease obstruction and the man was removed at 7.00 p.m. and sent to hospital, where he was pronounced to be dead. The Chapei policemen dispersed and the Settlement Police completed investigation into the accident.

The Commissioner of the Shanghai Municipal Police has protested to the Chief of the Public Safety Bureau against the action of the Chapei policemen, and requested him to issue orders that will prevent the occurrence of such an incident in the future.

上周六康纳路事件

闸北警察如何冷漠地阻止工部局警务处
警官救助重伤员；官方报告

以下是上海公共租界工部局新闻处发布的关于上周六晚引起广泛关注的康纳路事件的官方版本：

工部局警务处总监向工部局提交的报告指出，4月7日下午6时30分，戈登路巡捕房接到位于康纳路的中华公共汽车公司车场打来的电话，称康纳路车场附近发生事故，闸北警察在场并拒绝允许救火会救护车人员和公共汽车公司官员将一名伤者从公共汽车底下移出。副督察图洛克（Tulloch，音译）和副督察普里德莫尔（Pridmore，音译）立即赶赴现场，现场有一大群华人围观一辆公共汽车，其中包括约15名闸北警察。工部局警务处警官获悉，闸北警察拒绝允许救护车人员和公共汽车公司官员将伤者从车底移出，而在他们试图移出伤者时，该伤者仍然活着。

闸北警察介入

尽管副督察图洛克到达时认为该男子已死亡，但他仍指示救护车人员立即将该男子移出并送往医院。对此，闸北警察进行干预，阻止移出该男子。人们已采取措施用千斤顶抬起公共汽车以减轻压在男子身上的重量，尽管有闸北警察的阻挠，两位副督察仍试图移出该男子但未果。闸北警察声称他们在道路上拥有与租界警察同等的权利，坚持在收到其分区主管官员的命令之前不得移动尸体，并且必须先拍照。

手按手枪

此时，更多的闸北警察赶到，闸北警察与租界警察之间可能发生严重冲突。为避免冲突并移走伤者，副督察图洛克下令拍照。照片于下午6时58分拍摄，随后再次尝试移走该男子，但闸北警察情绪激动，推搡租界警察，其中多人以威胁的方式将手放在手枪上。随后收到消息，称闸北警察分区主管已命令其手下停止阻挠，该男子于下午7时被移出并送往医院，在医院被宣布死亡。闸北警察散去，租界警察完成了对事故的调查。

上海公共租界工部局警务处总监已向公安局局长抗议闸北警察的行为，并要求其发布命令，以防止此类事件今后再次发生。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, APRIL 11, 1934

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. & S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D 5794
Date 12 / 4 / 34

Serious Interference With
S.M. Police Functions

Native Police Refuse To Permit Injured Man To Be
Removed From Under Omnibus; Clash Of
Authority On Outside Road

Another of the numerous cases
of interference with the function-
ing of Municipal Police on the
Extra-Settlement Roads occurred
on Connaught Road, on Saturday
evening, and nearly precipitated
an open clash between members of
the Shanghai Municipal Police and
a number of Chinese police in the
vicinity of the China General
Omnibus Company. It is to the
credit of the Municipal Police
that they refrained under the
direct provocation from taking
direct action to assert their auth-
ority in a time of special emer-
gency, involving life and death.
Just what official action is to be
taken in the matter by the Shang-
hai Municipal Council has not been
disclosed, it being stated by S.M.C.
officials yesterday that the Coun-
cil "was awaiting a full report on
the matter."

Although for some time past
and since the case of detention of
a foreign woman by Chinese police
in the Western District, there
have been no reported instances
of interference by police of the
surrounding Chinese areas, Satur-
day's incident is undoubtedly one
of the worst of its kind for some
considerable time. That there was
not an open clash between the
representatives of the S.M.P. and
native police is solely due to the
forbearance of the men from Gor-
don Road Station. Menaced with
pistols held by the Chinese police
they were prevented from remov-
ing the body of an injured Chin-
ese from beneath the wheels
of a heavy 'bus, despite the
agony of the victim. For approx-
imately three quarters of an
hour the unfortunate man was
compelled to remain under the
'bus while the Chinese police
awaited instructions from a senior
officer and permission to take the
victim to hospital. In the mean-
time, the staff of the Fire
Brigade's Emergency Hospital
were forced to stand by and listen
to the dying groans of the injured
man, all attempts to extricate him
from beneath the 'bus being ob-
structed by the Chinese police.
When eventually the 'bus was
jacked up and the victim convey-
ed to hospital, he was found to
be dead.

Facts Of Case.

The facts of the case are briefly
these: Shortly after 6.20 p.m., on
Saturday evening, a 'bus owned
by the China General Omnibus
Company was involved in an ac-
cident which pinned a Chinese
beneath one of the wheels. The
accident occurred on Connaught
Road, near the Depot of the 'bus
company. A crowd quickly collected
and a number of Chinese police
appeared on the scene.

The efforts of the 'bus staff to
extricate the victim from beneath
the 'bus were prevented by the
Chinese police. A telephone
message was immediately sent to
Gordon Road Station and two for-
eign police officers proceeded to
the scene after summoning the
Emergency Ambulance.

The Chinese police refused to
allow the S.M.P. officer to remove
the injured man. Upon the ar-
rival of the Ambulance an attempt
was made to jack up the 'bus, but
again the Chinese police interfer-
ed. Asked for an explanation of
their actions the Chinese police
stated that they been instructed
to await orders from their senior
officers, adding that a photograph
of the accident must also be taken.

Removed Dead

Powerless to do anything short
of precipitating an open clash and
probably leading to bloodshed, the
S.M. Police officers awaited the
arrival of the photographer. A
few minutes before 7 o'clock a
flashlight picture was taken. But
it was not until about 10 minutes
later that orders were received
from some quarter which ended
the tension. The Chinese police
then permitted the 'bus to
be jacked up and the victim to be
removed. He was taken to hos-
pital but pronounced dead upon
arrival.

Conraught Road is one of the
Extra-Settlement Roads the con-
trol of which is at present in dis-
pute between the Shanghai Muni-
cipal Council and the Chinese
authorities. It has been the scene
of previous clashes between the
two authorities and serious trou-
ble has been narrowly averted.

Recently, assurances were given
by the Chinese authorities that
interference with the functioning
of the S. M. Police on outside
roads, and also with foreigners us-
ing them, would cease pending a
settlement of the present dispute.
Assurances were given by the
Chinese authorities that Chin-
ese police patrolling sections
along these roads had been in-
structed to refrain from inter-
ference with those lawfully using
these roads. Breaches of regula-
tions were to be reported to senior
officers, but Chinese police were
not to be permitted to interfere
with the functioning of Settlement
police on the roads in dis-
pute. For some time there has
been an absence of incidents on
extra-Settlement Roads, but Satur-
day's incident is one of the grav-
est that has been reported for
many months.

It is interesting to note, in this
connection, that Major-General
Wen Hun-gen, Chief of the Pub-
lic Safety Bureau, in a statement
issued yesterday to certain press-
men, flatly denied that the man
under the 'bus had been left there
is an injured condition. He stat-
ed that the victim had been killed
outright and that officers of the
Sixth District had sent for a
photographer to take a picture of
the accident as a basis for legal
action.

上海公共租界工部局警务处
刑事与特别 bureau 登记处。
编号 D 5794
日期 34年4月12日

严重干扰
工部局警务处职能

华捕拒绝允许将伤者从公共汽车下移走；越界筑路发生职权冲突

上周六晚，在康纳特路（Connaught Road）发生了又一起众多干扰工部局警察在越界筑路上执行职能的案件之一，险些导致上海公共租界巡捕（S.M.P.）成员与中国通用公共汽车公司附近的多名中国警察发生公开冲突。值得称道的是，工部局巡捕在面对直接挑衅时，克制住了采取直接行动以维护其权威的冲动，尽管当时处于涉及生死的特殊紧急关头。上海公共租界工部局（S.M.C.）将对此事采取何种官方行动尚未披露，工部局官员昨日称，工部局“正在等待关于此事的完整报告”。

虽然自西区华捕拘留一名外籍妇女一案以来，过去一段时间内未有周边华人区域警察进行干扰的报道，但周六的事件无疑是相当长一段时间以来最恶劣的一起此类事件。工部局巡捕代表与华捕之间未发生公开冲突，完全归功于戈登路捕房警员的克制。面对手持手枪威胁的中国警察，他们被阻止将一名受伤中国人的身体从重型公共汽车的车轮下移出，尽管受害者痛苦不堪。这名不幸的男子被迫在车下停留了大约四十五分钟，而中国警察则在等待上级军官的指示以及将受害者送往医院的许可。与此同时，消防队急诊医院的工作人员被迫在一旁站立，听着受伤者垂死的呻吟，所有试图将其从车下救出的尝试均遭到中国警察的阻挠。当最终公共汽车被千斤顶顶起并将受害者送医时，发现其已经死亡。

案件事实。

案件事实简述如下：上周六晚6点20分过后不久，一辆属于中国通用公共汽车公司的公共汽车卷入一起事故，将一名中国人压在一个车轮下。事故发生在康纳特路，靠近该公共汽车公司的车场。人群迅速聚集，多名中国警察出现在现场。

公共汽车工作人员试图将受害者从车下救出的努力被中国警察阻止。立即向戈登路捕房发送了电话消息，两名外籍警官在召唤急救救护车后前往现场。

中国警察拒绝允许工部局警官移走受伤男子。救护车到达后，曾试图用千斤顶顶起公共汽车，但中国警察再次进行干预。当被要求解释其行为时，中国警察称他们已接到指示等待上级军官的命令，并补充说必须对事故现场拍照。

移走时已死亡

除了引发公开冲突并可能导致流血事件外别无他法，工部局警官只得等待摄影师的到来。7点前几分钟拍摄了一张闪光灯照片。但直到大约10分钟后，才从某处收到结束紧张局势的命令。随后，中国警察允许将公共汽车顶起并移走受害者。他被送往医院，但抵达时被宣布死亡。

康纳特路是越界筑路之一，目前上海公共租界工部局与中国当局对其管辖权存在争议。此前双方当局曾在此发生过冲突，严重麻烦险些酿成。

最近，中国当局保证，在目前争端解决之前，将停止干扰工部局警察在界外道路上的职能行使，以及干扰使用这些道路的外国人。中国当局保证，沿这些道路巡逻路段的中国警察已接到指示，不得干扰合法使用这些道路的人员。违规行为应向上级军官报告，但不允许中国警察干扰租界警察在有争议道路上的职能行使。一段时间以来，越界筑路上未发生事故，但周六的事件是数月来报告的最严重事件之一。

值得注意的是，与此相关的是，公安局局长温亨根少将（Major-General Wen Hun-gen，音译）昨日向某些新闻界人士发表声明，断然否认车下的男子是在受伤状态下被留在那里的。他声称受害者当场死亡，第六区警官叫来摄影师拍摄事故照片，作为法律诉讼的依据。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, APRIL 11, 1934

'Torture Under Wheel'
Story Denied; Victim
Died At Once, Claim

A sensational story appearing in a morning paper concerning a pedestrian's alleged torture for 57 minutes in a bus accident on Connaught Road last Saturday evening and his death because of refusal by Public Safety Bureau officials to allow him to be moved to a hospital was flatly denied by Major-General Wen Hung-en, commissioner of the bureau, in an interview with The Shanghai Evening Post this morning.

"The pedestrian was killed outright," General Wen said. "It is because of the fact that he had been killed that officers of the Sixth District Bureau sent for a photographer to take a picture of the accident as basis for legal action."

General Wen issued the statement following personal investigation into the report. As motorcar accidents are ordinarily routine, he had not been informed of this particular mishap previously, it was understood.

"Foreign police and Chinese police are all the same," said the commissioner. "They are human beings. I could not imagine how one can believe in such a story that Chinese officers would leave a dying man under a wheel in order to take a picture. The Sixth District officer has told me that he has witnesses testifying that the pedestrian was killed outright."

（批：予收 孙 J）

《字林西报》，1934年4月11日，星期三

否认“车轮下受刑”
故事；声称受害者
当场死亡

今晨，《上海晚报》记者采访公安局局长温亨根少将时，他断然否认了一家晨报刊登的一则耸人听闻的故事。该故事称，上周六晚在康纳特路发生的一起公共汽车事故中，一名行人据称遭受了57分钟的折磨，并因公安局官员拒绝允许将其送往医院而死亡。

“该行人当场死亡，”温将军说。“正因为他已经死亡，第六区局的警官才叫来摄影师拍摄事故照片，作为法律诉讼的依据。”

据悉，温将军是在对该报道进行个人调查后发表此声明的。由于机动车事故通常属于常规事务，此前并未有人向他通报这起特定的不幸事故。

“外国警察和中国警察都是一样的，”局长说。“他们都是人。我无法想象人们怎么会相信这样的故事，即中国警官为了让一个垂死的人留在车轮下以便拍照。第六区警官告诉我，他有证人证明该行人是当场死亡的。”

（批：予收 孙 J）

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Tuesday, April 10, 1934

BUS ACCIDENT
A Reader's Amazement
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—Anyone not long conversant
with Chinese psychology, must have
read with amazement your account
this morning of the accident that
occurred on Connaught Road last
Saturday, where a human being was
forced by Chinese Police (on a
Municipal Council Road) to lie
screaming under the wheels of a bus,
while a photographer was summoned.
Fifty-seven minutes of agony, and then
a possibly unnecessary death, that the
wheels of a correct procedure as
conceived by a barbarous Chinese
officialdom might run its due course.
You state that the ten Settlement
police exercised a commendable
restraint, thus possibly forestalling a
nasty "incident." Personally, I am
sickened by the repetition of our
"forestalled incidents." I presume
the Municipal police had their orders,
and how I pity them, red-blooded
white men, forced to stand by for the
better part of an hour and watch a
fellow-mortal die by inches.
A GRAND STAND SEAT.
Shanghai, Apr. 10.

公共汽车事故
一位读者的惊愕
致《字林西报》编辑
先生，——任何不熟悉中国心理的人，读到今晨贵报关于上周六发生在康纳特路的事故报道时，必定感到惊愕。在该事故中，一个人被中国警察（在工部局道路上）强迫躺在公共汽车车轮下尖叫，同时召来摄影师。五十七分钟的痛苦，然后可能是本可避免的死亡，只为了让野蛮的中国官僚机构所构想的正确程序的车轮按其既定过程运转。您指出，十名租界警察表现出了值得称赞的克制，从而可能避免了一起令人不快的“事件”。就我个人而言，我对我们不断“避免的事件”感到厌恶。我推测工部局警察是接到了命令，我是多么同情他们，这些血气方刚的白人，被迫在一旁站立近一个小时，看着一个同类慢慢死去。
最佳观赛席。

Subject (in full) Report on Incident on Extra Settlement Roads.

Made by D.S.I. Moir Forwarded by

Sir,

I beg to report that a phone message was received
at this station at 6.30 p.m. 7/4/34 from the China General Omnibus
Company to the effect that an accident had occurred on Connaught
Road near The Bus Company premises. S.I.Tullock in company with
S.I.Pridmore immediately attended and ascertained that a male
Chinese riding a bicycle had been involved in a fatal accident.
The Fire Brigade Ambulance had already arrived on the scene and
instructions were given by S.I.Tullock to the officer in charge
of the Chapei Police who were in attendance to have the body
removed which he refused to do.

Interference then by Chapei Police was experienced
when S.I.Pridmore Mr. H.Haxley, China General Omnibus Coy, and
S.I. Tullock were threatened with pistols should the body be removed
without permitting them first to take a photograph of the acci-
dent.

Accordingly to the driver's statement and that of Mr.
A.Huxley deceased was alive after the accident, and if the Chapei
Police attached to the 6th Division had allowed the deceased to
be removed to hospital there may of been a chance of saving the
deceased life.

On the arrival of the undersigned and D.S.I.Tseu Han
Poo the body had been removed to the Public Mortuary pending an
inquest, and although enquiries were made amongst the crowd, that
gathered and residents in the vicinity, no witness to the accident
could be found.

Although I did not see the incident referred to by
S.I.Tullock and S.I.Pridmore, the Chapei Police were assisting
in dispersing the crowd which had gathered on the Municipal roadway.

谨报告，1934年4月7日下午6点30分，本站收到来自中国通用公共汽车公司的电话消息，称康纳特路靠近公共汽车公司 premises 处发生一起事故。二级督察塔尔洛克（S.I. Tullock）会同二级督察普里德莫尔（S.I. Pridmore）立即前往，查明一名骑自行车的中国男子卷入一起致命事故。消防队救护车已到达现场，二级督察塔尔洛克向在场的闸北警察负责人发出指令，要求移走尸体，但遭拒绝。

随后，当二级督察普里德莫尔、中国通用公共汽车公司的 H. Haxley 先生和二级督察塔尔洛克受到手枪威胁时，遭遇了闸北警察的干扰，威胁称若不允许他们先对事故拍照，便不得移走尸体。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, APRIL 10, 1934
8314

CONNAUGHT ROAD INCIDENT
Chinese Prevent Removal Of Accident Victim
KEPT UNDER BUS UNTIL PHOTOGRAPH TAKEN

Another serious incident which occurred on one of the contested outside roads has just come to light.
On Saturday last, at about 6 p.m., a young Chinese was knocked down and pinned under the wheel of one of the China General Omnibus Co.'s busses running along Connaught Road. The accident occurred almost opposite the bus company's depot. Immediate aid was summoned and a call put in for the emergency ambulance of the Shanghai Fire Brigade.
The Chapei police were immediately on the scene and when the ambulance arrived, six minutes after the accident, they prevented the man from being removed from under the wheel. During the whole of this time the man was alive and shrieking from the pain. When the Chapei police could not be prevailed upon to remove the man a call was put in to the Gordon Road police station of the Shanghai Municipal Police. Three officers from the station were soon on the scene.

Chapei Police Prevent Removal
When further attempts were made to assist the victim, the Chapei police again intervened and prevented any attempt at rescue. They insisted that the man remain where he was, under the wheel of the bus, until a photographer could be summoned to take a picture of the accident.
Reinforcements were called from the Settlement police force and these soon arrived. On their arrival, however, the Chapei police became definitely menacing in their attitude and only very commendable restraint on the part of the Settlement police prevented a very ugly incident.
Eventually the photographer arrived and took a flashlight photograph of the accident. Only then would the Chapei police allow the victim to be removed, some 57 minutes after the accident had taken place. The man was pronounced dead upon being removed, the verdict by the doctors being death through injuries and shock.
Traffic was blocked on Connaught Road for more than three quarters of an hour during which the more than twenty Chapei police on hand did nothing to clear the area. At first only three Settlement police turned out in answer to the call and on the second call being put in the total number was increased to ten.

Police Officer Pushed Over
During the incident the attitude of the Chapei police was distinctly unpleasant. Sub-Inspector Pridmore, one of the Settlement officers, was pushed over by one of the Chapei police who interfered while the Settlement officer was attempting to remove the injured man and place him on a Fire Brigade stretcher. When he regained his feet two or three of the Chinese police were seen to place their hands on their pistols.
A crowd of about 800 people constituted another difficulty for the Settlement police and angry shouts were heard on all sides but the Chapei sub-inspector was successful in preventing any disturbance. The injured man, however, was kept under the bus until a Chinese photographer in Bubbling Well Road was able to get on the scene on instructions of the Chapei police and take a photograph of the bus, the bicycle and the victim.
It is understood that the China General Omnibus Company is forwarding a report on the affair to the Shanghai Municipal Council.

康纳特路事件
华人阻挠移走事故受害者
直至拍照完毕方将其从车下移出

又一起发生在争议界外道路上的严重事件刚刚曝光。
上周六下午6时许，一名年轻华人在康纳特路（Connaught Road）被英商中国公共汽车公司（China General Omnibus Co.）的一辆公交车撞倒，并被压在车轮之下。事故地点几乎正对该公交公司的车场。当局立即寻求援助，并呼叫上海救火会的紧急救护车。
闸北警察随即赶到现场，当救护车在事故发生六分钟后抵达时，他们阻止将该男子从车轮下移出。在此期间，该男子一直活着，并因疼痛而尖叫。由于无法说服闸北警察移走该男子，遂向上海公共租界工部局警务处戈登路（Gordon Road）巡捕房报案。该巡捕房的三名警员很快赶到了现场。

闸北警察阻挠移走伤者
当再次尝试救助受害者时，闸北警察再次介入，阻止任何救援企图。他们坚持要求该男子留在原地，即公交车轮下，直到召来摄影师对事故现场进行拍照。
租界警力被调派增援，并很快到达。然而，他们的到来使闸北警察的态度变得明显具有威胁性，只是由于租界警察表现出值得高度赞扬的克制，才避免了一起极为恶劣的事件。
最终，摄影师赶到，并对事故现场进行了闪光灯拍照。至此，闸北警察才允许移走受害者，此时距事故发生已过去约57分钟。该男子被移出后被宣布死亡，医生的验断结论为因受伤和休克致死。
康纳特路的交通阻塞了超过三刻钟，在此期间，在场的二十多名闸北警察未采取任何措施疏导区域。起初，响应呼叫出动的租界警察仅有三人，在第二次发出呼叫后，总人数增加至十人。

警员被推倒
在事件过程中，闸北警察的态度显然令人不快。租界警员之一的副督察普里德莫尔（Pridmore）在试图将伤者移至救火会担架时，遭到一名闸北警察的干扰并被推倒。当他重新站稳时，可以看到两三名华捕将手放在了手枪上。
约800人组成的围观人群给租界警察带来了另一重困难，四周可听到愤怒的叫喊声，但闸北副督察成功防止了任何骚乱的发生。然而，该伤者一直被留在公交车下，直到一名位于静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）的华人摄影师按照闸北警察的指示赶到现场，并对公交车、自行车和受害者拍了照。
据悉，英商中国公共汽车公司正在就此事向上海公共租界工部局提交报告。
